title: Formal and regular Taylor rank-minor ideals
statement: Let $\sigma$ be a finite variable type. Put $E_t=\{\delta\in\mathbf N^{(\sigma)}:|\delta|\le t\}$ and $\delta!=\prod_j\delta_j!$. Reindex a finite matrix $M$ over a commutative ring $R$ by $\operatorname{Fin}$ and write $J_r(M)$ for its $r$-minor ideal [def-trf-minor-ideal]. For a field $L$ and a finite list $f_i\in L[[X_j:j\in\sigma]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], define $B_t(f)$ with rows $\delta\in E_t$, columns $(i,\eta)\in\operatorname{Fin}(s)\times E_t$, entry $(\delta-\eta)!^{-1}\partial^{\delta-\eta}f_i$ when $\eta\le\delta$, and zero otherwise. Use the formal partial derivatives [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative] and their iterates in the finite enumeration order of [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum]. Define $r_t(f)=\operatorname{rank}_L B_t(f)(0)$, $J_t(f)=J_{r_t(f)+1}(B_t(f))$ and $J_{\le q}(f)=\sum_{t=0}^qJ_t(f)$. For $\alpha_i\in\mathbf N^n$ and $f_i\in L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m,Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]]$, set $E(\alpha,f)=(\partial^\nu f_i:|\nu|<|\alpha_i|)$. For a field $k$, a commutative ring $B$, a ring map $c:k[x_j:j\in\sigma]\to B$, specified $\mathbf Z$-derivations $D_j:B\to B$, and a finite list $h_i\in B$, define $D^\delta h$ by applying each $D_j$ exactly $\delta_j$ times in that same finite enumeration order. Let $P_t(c,D,h)$ have rows $\delta\in E_t$, columns $(i,\eta)$ as above, and entry $c((\delta-\eta)!^{-1})D^{\delta-\eta}h_i$ when $\eta\le\delta$, zero otherwise. For a field $L$ and ring map $\mathrm{ev}:B\to L$, define $J_t(c,D,h;\mathrm{ev})=J_{\operatorname{rank}_L\mathrm{ev}(P_t)+1}(P_t)$. Factorials are mapped to the relevant field before taking inverses. These are constructions without a characteristic or coordinate-existence assertion. Empty variable or generator families, zero ranks, full ranks and oversized minors are included.

source.place: BM 1997 Definitions 7.9, 7.12--7.13, Theorem 7.14 and Remarks 9.1, 9.5, pp.265--268,275--277; finite Taylor matrices and derivative ideals used in completion of Theorem 9.6, p.282. ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the route reference.
